features.name: any_comment_links_major_news_domain
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a link to a recognized news or media organization?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; if missing/malformed return null; empty list gives 0. Return 1 if any comment contains a URL (http/https or www.) whose hostname (lowercased, with subdomains allowed) equals or ends with '.'+ one of this fixed list: nytimes.com, theguardian.com, guardian.co.uk, bbc.com, bbc.co.uk, reuters.com, apnews.com, washingtonpost.com, wsj.com, cnn.com, npr.org, bloomberg.com, economist.com, ft.com, nbcnews.com, cbsnews.com, abcnews.go.com, usatoday.com, latimes.com, time.com, theatlantic.com, newyorker.com, foxnews.com, politico.com, aljazeera.com, pbs.org. Else 0. Raw text match; no semantic filtering. Comment text may contain outcome announcements; not outcome-free.

h0: any_comment_links_major_news_domain has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Discussions with a counter-argument linking to a recognized news organization have a higher rate of OP view change.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change) at discussion level; comment-level persuasion is unavailable. "Recognized news and media organizations" is operationalized as a fixed domain list (the "etc." is unspecified, so the list is an assumption and not exhaustive). Link presence is only detected in OC_comments text; shortened URLs or unlinked citations are missed. Comment text may contain outcome announcements; the raw match does not filter them. Association only, not causal.
